deities: Lord Panchmukhi Hanuman (five-faced Hanuman: Hanuman, Narasimha, Garuda, Varaha, Hayagriva)

history.period: Modern - established 1978 (per the temple's official website)
history.summary: The CSV town 'Yamunanagar' is imprecise - the temple is actually in Vill. Basatian Wala (Dhaka Basatiyan Wala), near Bilaspur on the Bilaspur-Chhachhrauli Road, about 4 km from Bilaspur, in Yamunanagar district. According to the temple's official website, it was established in 1978 and has grown into a prominent regional shrine of Panchmukhi Hanuman, the five-faced form of Lord Hanuman (Hanuman facing east, Narasimha south, Garuda west, Varaha north, Hayagriva upward). Local tradition holds that the five Pandavas visited this place and worshipped Hanuman in his five-faced form; one folk account says this is where Hanuman assumed the Panchamukha form to kill the demon Ahiravana and rescue Rama and Lakshmana (standard Panchamukhi legend, attached to this site locally - treat as legend, not history). The temple hosts an annual Maha Jagran, weekly Sundarkand path, and daily aartis, drawing large Tuesday crowds.

name: Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir
town_description: Bilaspur is a town in Yamunanagar district of Haryana, about 15 km from Yamunanagar city on the route toward Chhachhrauli and the Shivalik foothills. It is an agricultural market town serving surrounding villages and a gateway to the Kalesar forest region. The town is best known outside the district for the Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir nearby.

travel.road: On Bilaspur-Chhachhrauli Road, 4 km from Bilaspur/Vyaspur; buses and cabs from Yamunanagar, Ambala and Chandigarh

visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 5:00 AM - 12:00 PM; Evening 4:00 PM - 9:00 PM; Tuesdays open all day (per temple's official website)
